# Hash-pinned install set for the BrowserStack cross-browser job.
#
# Direct requirements: flask pytest pytest-playwright requests browserstack-sdk
#
# Used by browserstack.yml's "Install dependencies" step. That step ran a bare
# `pip install flask pytest pytest-playwright requests browserstack-sdk`, so
# every run resolved whatever the index served that minute -- and this job
# holds BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME / BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY, which is exactly the
# kind of job an unpinned resolve should not be feeding.
#
# Installed with `pip install --require-hashes`, which refuses to install
# anything not listed here with a matching hash -- so the job gets the exact
# artifacts this file names, or it fails. Every transitive dependency is
# present because --require-hashes demands the whole closure; that is the
# point, not padding. The closure is large because browserstack-sdk pulls in
# Selenium, Appium and Robot Framework of its own accord.
#
# Each version lists the sha256 of EVERY distribution PyPI publishes for it
# (wheels for each platform, plus the sdist). pip accepts a download that
# matches any one of them, so the pin does not quietly depend on the runner
# resolving to the same wheel this file was generated against.
#
# browserstack-sdk publishes no wheel, so pip builds it from the sdist named
# here. That was already true of the unpinned install; what changes is that
# the sdist is now hash-checked before anything is built from it.
#
# Generated on Linux / CPython 3.11, matching the job's runner
# (ubuntu-latest) and its actions/setup-python version. Resolution is
# interpreter-dependent; do not reuse this file for another interpreter.
#
# Regenerate with:
#   pip-compile --generate-hashes --strip-extras --no-header \
#     --output-file=.github/requirements/browserstack.txt <the names above>
#
# Kept moving by the `/.github/requirements` Dependabot entry, which groups
# this directory into one weekly PR and rewrites the --hash lines along with
# the versions. The pin makes an upgrade deliberate; that entry is what keeps
# it from going stale.
